Day 27: Iran–Israel campaign — latest (last 30 min)

  • Diplomacy / Politics
  • Trump announced a 2nd pause on Iran energy strikes — 10 days, expires Apr 6, 2026 8 PM ET. He says talks are "going very well." Iran denies direct talks.
  • US Congress action: 22 Democrats joined GOP to block a War Powers resolution on Lebanon. That removes a US legal constraint on support for Netanyahu and reduces chances Washington forces a ceasefire.
  • Airspace & Mobility
  • Flight-scan snapshot: 348 aircraft, 0 military detected. Civilian airports closed across the region: Iran, Israel, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Jordan. Tactical note: region-wide closures disrupt evacuations and civilian logistics; military likely using non-public air corridors and sea routes.
  • Military Operations
  • Campaign continues: Israeli/US airstrikes on Iranian targets vs Iranian/Hezbollah/Hamas missile strikes on Israel. Northern border (Hezbollah) active daily.
  • Tactical context: first pause was violated hours after it began (Isfahan, Khorramshahr strikes). Pause durability is uncertain.
  • Straits & Shipping
  • Iran allows Hormuz passage for select states (Russia, India, China) and blocks others. This skews shipping and energy routes; raises insurance and diversion costs.
  • Mediation
  • Pakistan is acting as intermediary. No confirmed breakthrough reported.
  • 🟢 Good News: A formal 10-day pause on energy strikes is in effect for now. Public flight-scan shows no military aircraft.
  • Threat assessment: Escalating.

Situation Report — Day 27 (last 6h)

  • Active strikes/sirens: Ongoing US/Israeli airstrikes on Iran. Daily Hezbollah/IRGC/Hamas missile and rocket strikes on Israel’s north and south.
  • Pause & Diplomacy: Trump announced a 10-day pause on energy strikes until Apr 6, 2026 8:00 PM ET, citing an “Iranian government request.” Iran denies direct talks. Pakistan is mediating. Qatar’s PM met US envoys; Doha says negotiations continue without senior-level meetings.

  • Northern Border: Hezbollah activity continues daily. Israel has struck targets in Lebanon this cycle. High risk of sustained rocket/ground exchanges.
  • Maritime / Hormuz: Iran allows passage for friendly states (Russia, India, China). Other flagged vessels face restrictions.
  • Airspace & flights: Major regional airports remain closed (Iran, Israel, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Jordan). Civil aviation sharply reduced.
  • Economics & energy: Iran reports resumed oil exports after US blockade lift; parliament speaker cites >40m barrels exported and ~20% rise in Iranian oil prices.
  • Domestic politics: US congressional move blocked a Lebanon war-powers resolution, easing Israeli operational freedom. Netanyahu reiterates pursuit of “total victory.”
  • 🟢 Good News: 10-day pause on energy strikes announced. Pakistan and Qatar engaged in mediation — a diplomatic window for de-escalation.

Threat assessment: Escalating

Situation Report — Day 27

  • Pauses & diplomacy
    • Trump announced a SECOND pause on US strikes against Iranian energy infrastructure: 10 days (deadline 6 Apr 2026, 20:00 ET). He said Iran requested it; Tehran denies direct talks.
    • First pause (5 days, Mar 23) was violated hours later when US/Israeli jets struck Isfahan and Khorramshahr — shows pauses are fragile.
    • Pakistan acting as mediator. Qatar says negotiations continue but without high-level direct talks.
  • Air / sea / airspace
    • Regional airspace largely closed: airports reported closed in Iran, Israel, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Jordan. Passenger traffic down sharply.
    • Iran allows passage through Hormuz for Russia, India, China; blocks others — tactical lifeline for friendly states and economic pressure relief.
    • Military flights detected (e.g., RCH535, C-130). Ongoing air operations reported by both sides.
  • Northern border (Hezbollah)
    • Daily Hezbollah activity continues. Netanyahu visited south Lebanon, vowed IDF will not withdraw while Hezbollah remains — signals continued ground pressure and limited ceasefire prospects.
  • Strike/counterstrike pattern
    • Conflict remains a tit-for-tat cycle: US/Israeli airstrikes on Iranian targets and Iranian/proxy missile strikes toward Israel continue.
  • International military moves
    • Turkey reopened talks on Patriot and SAMP/T missile defenses with NATO — increased regional air-defense coordination likely.
  • Domestic / political
    • US congressional action: 22 Democrats joined Republicans to block a Lebanon War Powers resolution (reported) — reduces a congressional check on broader regional operations.
    • Netanyahu rhetoric remains maximalist: “pursuit of total victory.”
  • 🟢 Good News
    • Pause announcement, Pakistan mediation and reopened NATO missile-defense talks create diplomatic openings that could reduce escalation if sustained.
  • Threat assessment: Escalating.

48.en:
Situation Report — Day 27 (last 48h)

  • ACTIVE STRIKES/SIRENS: Israel and US continue airstrikes on Iranian targets. Iran, Hezbollah and Gaza factions keep launching ballistic/missile strikes at Israel. Northern border active daily.
  • Pause announced: Trump declared a 2nd pause on strikes targeting Iranian energy for 10 days (deadline Apr 6, 2026 8 PM ET), saying talks are “going very well.” Iran denies direct talks. First 5-day pause (Mar 23) was breached by US/Israeli strikes on Isfahan and Khorramshahr.
  • Diplomacy: Pakistan mediating. Qatar says negotiations continue without high-level meetings. No confirmed breakthrough.
  • Northern Border: Hezbollah firing daily. PM Netanyahu visited southern Lebanon and signaled continued IDF presence while Hezbollah operates.
  • Air/Sea & infrastructure: Regional commercial airports closed across Iran, Israel, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Jordan. Military flights observed (RCH535, C-130, IAF274). Iran allows passage through Hormuz for Russia, India, China; blocks others.
  • International military posture: Turkey reopened talks on Patriot and SAMP/T missile defense systems with NATO partners. Germany reconsidering air-defense posture in region.
  • Energy/economics: Iran reports resumed oil exports and higher oil prices after sanctions suspension. Financial access disputes (Qatar-held funds) unresolved.
  • Domestic politics: US pause and Congressional moves complicate US domestic consensus on authorization for war powers in Lebanon/region.
  • Operational note: Pauses fragile—previous pause violated within hours. Iran’s proxy network continues asymmetric missile and drone strikes into Israel.
  • 🟢 Good News: A temporary pause is in place and mediators (Pakistan, Qatar) remain engaged.
  • Threat assessment: Escalating — high chance of localized strikes breaking pauses and wider retaliation.

  • דיפלומטיה: פעריס מתווכת; קטאר מדווחת ששיחות נמשכות ללא מפגשים ברמת שרים. אין פריצת דרך מאומתת.

  • תעופה וים: נמלי תעופה אזוריים סגורים - איראן, ישראל, עיראק, סוריה, לבנון, ירדן. תצפיות על טיסות צבאיות (RCH535, C-130, IAF274). איראן מאפשרת מעבר הורמוז לרוסיה, הודו וסין; חוסמת אחרים.

  • הערכת איום: מתגבר — סבירות גבוהה להפרת הפסקות אש ולתגמולים מקומיים והרחבת סכסוך.
